channel.title: RSS Aggregator Feed
channel.description: An aggregated feed of Technology-related news

item.title: Apple updates Final Cut Camera to support the iPhone 18 Pro's variable aperture
item.description: The company is also rolling out new features across several of its Creator Studio apps.

item.title: Mozilla deploys a new-look Firefox across desktop and mobile
item.description: The redesigned browser brings back compact mode and adds a theme picker.

item.title: OpenAI’s latest features take direct aim at the app store model
item.description: OpenAI is building out the pieces of an alternative to the traditional app store model, turning ChatGPT into a place where software can be discovered and used by people and AI agents alike.

item.title: Could Google kick out Russian apps from Android for good? A new developer verification system may be the first step towards a total ban for Moscow developers, almost 56 months since the start of the Ukraine war
item.description: Russia fears Google’s Android developer verification could make Russian applications harder to install.

item.title: Attention, Brick users: You can now personalize your phone lock with colorful cases
item.description: Brick has launched color cases for its viral screen time phone lock device. They cost $39 each and come in four colors.

item.title: The biggest announcements from OpenAI DevDay: Dots, GPT-6.1 Sol, Ultrafast
item.description: OpenAI unveiled quite a few new products at DevDay 2026, including GPT-6.1 Sol and a new AI agent system called Dots.

item.title: OpenAI repotedly in talks to raise $30B round at $1.4T valuation
item.description: The new round is anticipated to be the company's last before its delayed 2027 public debut.

item.title: Google partners with known nerd Henry Cavill on a video game to showcase Googlebooks
item.description: The final result will be published in November.

item.title: I found the best iPhone 18 Pro cases and grips to protect your new phone
item.description: The newest iPhones are here. I went searching for the best iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max cases from Otterbox, Apple, Popsockets, and more.

item.title: OpenAI’s new dots agent comes with a crew of friendly mascots
item.description: You’d trust a frog named Todd, right? OpenAI just announced a new suite of AI agents called “dots,” and they look like something you might find in an animated kids show.

item.title: Amazon is spending $20 million to support water conservation on the Colorado River — but still won't say how much water it uses
item.description: Amazon is investing $20 million to save Colorado River water, but how much of that river it uses remains opaque at best.

item.title: OpenAI introduces Dots, a new always-on AI agent, at Dev Day 2026
item.description: At OpenAI's annual developer conference, the company made 20 different announcements, but none bigger than the new AI agent, Dots.

item.title: Xbox just unveiled Mythic Achievements, which are basically PlayStation platinum trophies
item.description: They signal to the world that someone has fully completed a game. And they apply retroactively to titles you've already finished.

item.title: OpenAI Gets Sued Over the Hugging Face Hack
item.description: A nonprofit in California is doing what Hugging Face has not—attempting to hold OpenAI legally accountable for the actions of its agents.

item.title: A family almost let their dad sleep through a stroke, until ChatGPT told them to get help
item.description: Some alarming ChatGPT stories show why AI may be most valuable in healthcare when it recognizes danger and tells you when to get human help

item.title: U.S. workers spend nearly $7,000 per year just to show up at the office
item.description: Surprisingly, the same study found that the ‘RTO Tax’ is lowest in some of the country’s most expensive cities, including New York, Boston, and San Francisco, once salary is factored in. American workers spend an average of $6,736 each year just to show up at the office, according to a recent study by resume-building platform Resume.io.

item.title: Meta’s new AI agent gave a stranger a user’s home address. Then he showed up
item.description: A Facebook Marketplace buyer arrived at a seller’s home after Meta’s Muse AI agent handled the deal and shared pickup information. Another day, another AI agent gone rogue.

item.title: 24 heures après avoir annulé Astra, OpenAI lance GPT-6.1 Sol, classé « critique » en cybersécurité
item.description: En vingt-quatre heures, OpenAI a rangé au placard son prochain modèle de pointe pour excès de risque, puis mis en vente une déclinaison presque aussi capable, cinq fois moins chère, et officiellement classée « critique » en cybersécurité.

item.title: Acemagic K5 mini PC review
item.description: The Acemagic K5 uses the new Intel Wild Lake processor that replaces the older N-series chips. but it's a case of new technology, same underlying limitations.

item.title: More Ways to Disrupt: New 2026 Side Events from KOTRA, WayFounder, Enterprise Ireland, SafetyWing + Descope
item.description:
Disrupt doesn’t end when you leave Moscone West. 👀
Founder dinners, investor meetups, happy hours, workshops, roundtables and more are taking over San Francisco during Disrupt Week.
See what’s happening, find your people, and start building your calendar.

item.title: Singapore pilots a government-built dating service
item.description: Singapore's GovTech is piloting FirstDate, a Singpass-verified matchmaking service for public officers amid record-low births.

item.title: Apple Pay set to launch in India with Axis Bank today, sources say
item.description: Some of India's largest banks are holding off on supporting Apple Pay initially.

item.title: There's now an official US government AI chatbot
item.description: The administration wants America.gov to be the main portal for federal services.

item.title: « Se connecter avec ChatGPT » : votre abonnement OpenAI devient un moyen de dépenser des tokens
item.description: Avec « Se connecter avec ChatGPT », OpenAI permet d'utiliser les tokens de son abonnement dans des applications tierces. Seize partenaires au lancement, et une facture IA qui ne se dédouble plus. Le quota, lui, va fondre plus vite.

item.title: Here’s why OpenAI is absent from Nvidia’s industry-wide effort to end rogue AI agents
item.description: OpenAI isn't a public supporter of Nvidia's Open Agent Safety Platform, but it is privately working with Nvidia, TechCrunch has learned.
